faqs.question: Should I ask her parents before or after I propose to my girlfriend?
faqs.answer: Ask her first, then her parents, usually within a week. Going to the parents first turns her into the last person consulted about her own marriage, and the 2026 rural Maharashtra study found only 15.5% of women were the primary decision-maker on who they married — the imbalance is already there without you adding to it.

faqs.question: What if she says yes but her parents say no?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a timeline problem, not a verdict. Agree with her on which specific objection is being made — caste, city, income, timing — and who in the family actually holds the decision, then set a review date so the refusal has an end rather than drifting.

faqs.question: Do I need a ring to propose for marriage in India?
faqs.answer: No. A ring is a Western convention that many Indian families fold into the engagement ceremony rather than the private ask, so a ring at the private moment is optional and sometimes premature. What she needs from the private ask is a clear question and something she can show her family.

faqs.question: Is it fine to propose over a link or a page instead of in person?
faqs.answer: It works when you cannot be in the same room, and it works badly as a substitute for a conversation she has asked for in person. Across SubhSandesh's whole platform, 48.9% of page views happen on a phone (25,167 of 51,504), so a page reaches her wherever she is — but it is a delivery format, not a replacement for presence.

faqs.question: What should I actually say when I propose for marriage?
faqs.answer: Say what you have decided rather than what you feel: the year you want to marry in, where you would live, and what you will do if a family objects. Feelings she already knows; a plan is the new information, and it is the part she will repeat to her parents.

faqs.question: What is a roka and does it replace the proposal?
faqs.answer: A roka is a North Indian ceremony that formalises a match and opens the engagement period. A 2025 Journal of Marriage and Family study of 48 Delhi-area interviews found couples in self-chosen relationships using it to signal parental endorsement — so it follows the private ask rather than replacing it.

faqs.question: How long should I wait between proposing and telling the families?
faqs.answer: Days, not months. The longer the private yes sits unshared, the more likely it reaches a parent through a cousin or a screenshot, which starts the family conversation defensively.

faqs.question: Is Propose Day the right day to ask for marriage?
faqs.answer: Propose Day 2027 falls on Monday 8 February, the second day of Valentine week, which makes it a working day in most of India. That narrows the window for anything that needs an evening or a family visit, so pick the weekend either side unless the date itself matters to her.

faqs.question: How private is a page I send her?
faqs.answer: Only as private as the link, unless you lock it. 39.9% of SubhSandesh creators platform-wide password-protect a page before sharing it (1,822 of 4,567), which is the setting that matters when phones get passed around a living room.

faqs.question: How long does it take to make a proposal page?
faqs.answer: Longer than the ten minutes people budget. The median gap between a page's first save and its last edit is 6.4 hours — a figure sampled on the "I love you" template with n=1,138, not on proposals, since no proposal-page measurement exists.

faqs.question: What if I already asked and she said not yet?
faqs.answer: Do not re-stage the same proposal. Find out whether the objection is timing, family or the relationship itself, and if the last attempt ended in a fight, deal with the fight on its own before asking again.

article.contentMarkdown:
# How to Propose Girlfriend for Marriage When Two Families Decide

Propose in two stages: ask her privately first, in a form she can keep and re-read, then take the same question to both families in the order they expect. That second stage is not a courtesy in India — in the 2005 India Human Development Survey only 4.94% of women described their marriage as fully self-arranged, while 36.52% described the choice as jointly made with their parents. The private ask still carries the weight, and it takes longer to build than most people plan for: across SubhSandesh's whole platform, 4,567 personalised pages have been created since 12 March 2026 across 16 page types, and the median gap between a page's first save and its last edit is 6.4 hours — a figure sampled on the "I love you" template with n=1,138, not on proposals. Below: the order of the ask, what Indian survey data says about who decides, and what to do in the gap between her yes and theirs.

## What a marriage proposal means in India when two families are involved

A marriage proposal in India is usually two asks separated by days or weeks: a private question to your partner, and a negotiation between two households that converts her answer into a wedding date. The Western script collapses both into one knee-down moment. The Indian one rarely does.

The second stage has its own machinery. In North India a *roka* formalises a match and opens the engagement period, and a 2025 study in the *Journal of Marriage and Family*, based on 48 interviews in the Delhi area, found couples in self-chosen relationships using the roka specifically to signal that their match had parental endorsement — a way of avoiding stigma rather than a wedding admin step.

This shape is not an Indian peculiarity. An ethnographic study published in *Frontiers in Sociology* in March 2026 describes *warmi urquy* in Huanta, Peru, a marriage proposal staged between two families and their godparents rather than between the couple.

So "how do I propose" is really three questions in a fixed order: what do I say to her, what do I say to her parents, and when do I say it to mine.

## Who actually decides, according to Indian survey data

Less of this is up to the two of you than the proposal-video genre suggests. Manjistha Banerji's 2008 analysis of the India Human Development Survey (N = 20,854 women who married between ages 15 and 24) found the single most common answer was not "my parents chose" and not "I chose" — it was **jointly arranged, at 36.52%**, just ahead of parent-arranged with no consent at 35.36%. Parent-arranged *with* the woman's consent accounted for 23.18%, and only 4.94% reported a fully self-arranged marriage.

More recent, more local data says the same thing harder. A 2026 study in *Contraception and Reproductive Medicine*, surveying 1,192 married women aged 18–30 in rural Maharashtra, found 15.5% were the primary decision-maker on **who** they married and 9.4% on **when**. The most common primary decision-makers on partner choice were uncles (29.8%) and fathers (20.8%); on timing, fathers decided in 66.0% of cases.

The practical reading: a proposal aimed only at her is aimed at roughly the smallest share of the decision. Plan the family conversation as a stage of the proposal, not as paperwork that follows it.

## The order of the ask: five steps that decide whether the yes holds

### 1. Settle the whether before you stage the when

A proposal should surprise her with the date, never with the question. Ask directly whether she wants to marry you within the next year or two, and whether her family knows you exist.

Banerji's data shows how thin the contact assumption can be: even among women reporting a self-arranged marriage, 38.97% had met their husband on the wedding day itself. If she has never named you at home, the proposal is the wrong instrument — a conversation is.

### 2. Ask her alone, in something she can keep

Do the private ask with no audience and no staff. Say what you have decided about the next ten years, not what you feel about the last three; specificity is what makes it real. Leave her something re-readable, because she will need to describe it to her mother within forty-eight hours.

This is exactly the job the [SubhSandesh "Will You Marry Me?" proposal page](/proposal) was built for — a scrapbook of your story ending in a YES button that grows every time she dodges it, on a link only she has. Across the platform as a whole, 39.9% of creators password-protect a page before sharing it (1,822 of 4,567), which is what keeps a private thing private in a household where phones get handed around.

### 3. Ask her parents in the format they expect

Within a week of her yes, ask her how her parents want to be approached — a visit, a call from your parents, or a meal. Do not improvise this.

In the rural Maharashtra sample above, the person who most often decided the partner was not the father but an uncle, at 29.8%, so "I'll speak to her dad" can miss the actual decision-maker entirely. Ask her who genuinely has to be persuaded, and go to that person.

### 4. Bring your own family in before they hear it secondhand

Tell your parents before the news travels. A proposal that reaches your mother through a cousin's WhatsApp forward starts the family conversation in a defensive position, and 48.9% of all page views on SubhSandesh happen on a phone (25,167 of 51,504 views platform-wide) — anything you send is one screenshot away from a group chat. Give your side the version you want repeated.

### 5. Put a date on it, or the yes drifts

Convert the yes into something dated within a month: a roka, an engagement, a meeting between families, even a fixed month for the wedding. The 2025 Delhi study found that courtship during the engagement period sometimes ends in a broken engagement, which is a real risk to name rather than a reason to rush. An undated yes is the version that quietly expires.

## Four ways to make the private ask, compared

These are the four formats people actually choose for the private half of the proposal, with what each costs and who else can see it.

| Way of asking | What it costs you in time | Who else can see it | What SubhSandesh's own data says |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spoken, in private, no props | One evening | No one | No proposal-page data exists — this is unmeasured |
| Public setup at a restaurant or mall | Days of booking and coordination | Waiting staff, other diners, anyone filming | Unmeasured |
| A private page you build and send as a link | Median 6.4 hours from first save to last edit, sampled on the /love-gf template, n=1,138 | Only whoever has the link; 39.9% of creators platform-wide add a password | 92.7% of started pages platform-wide are finished and shared (4,234 of 4,567) |
| Family-first: roka or a meeting before you ask her | Weeks of scheduling between two households | Both families, by design | Unmeasured |

The honest takeaway: the page format wins on privacy control and on being re-readable, and loses to the spoken ask on immediacy. None of the SubhSandesh figures above are proposal-specific — every one is platform-wide across 16 page types or sampled on the "I love you" template, because no proposal-page measurement exists.

## The gap between her yes and their yes

Most guides stop at the yes. The gap after it is where Indian proposals actually fail, and it usually lasts weeks.

Use it for three things. Agree what you will both say about how you met — the 2025 Delhi research describes couples using the engagement to present a self-chosen match as an endorsed one.

Second, agree the non-negotiables you will not trade for approval: city, career, timeline. Third, set a review date, so "they need more time" has an end.

There is also a shift working in your favour. A 2025 study in *Social Forces* of unmarried, partnered women across twenty Indian states found that daily internet use — and specifically owning the device rather than sharing it — was associated with more secular views on partner choice and on love marriage. The generation being asked has moved further than the generation being consulted.

## When a proposal page is the wrong call

If the two of you are already effectively engaged and the families are already talking, a solemn scrapbook overshoots. A couple who run on jokes will get more out of [the Court of Love, where you put your partner on trial with a penguin judge](/court-of-love) than out of a page that asks a question everybody already answered. Match the register to the relationship, not to the occasion.

Skip the digital route entirely in three cases. If she has told you she wants the question asked in person and nothing else, a link is a downgrade. If her parents are the primary audience for the first conversation, a page aimed at her does not touch the decision the Maharashtra data says her uncle or father is making.

And if you are asking again after a refusal or a fight, a proposal page is the wrong shape — an [apology page that deals with the fight first](/apology-dashboard) is the honest order of operations.

One more limit worth stating plainly: SubhSandesh has no data on proposal pages at all. Every number on this page is platform-wide across 16 page types or sampled on the "I love you" template, and none of it should be read as a claim about how proposals specifically perform.

## Sources

- Manjistha Banerji, *Is Education Associated with a Transition towards Autonomy in Partner Choice? A Case Study of India*, University of Maryland, 2008 — [full text in DRUM](https://drum.lib.umd.edu/handle/1903/8809)
- Anita Raj et al., *Measuring marital choice as an indicator of women's marital agency in rural India*, **Contraception and Reproductive Medicine**, 2026 — [open access](https://contraceptionmedicine.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s40834-026-00437-z)
- Megan Reed, *Roka Engagements and the Hybridization of Arranged and "Love" Marriage in Urban India*, **Journal of Marriage and Family**, May 2025 — [abstract](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/jomf.13115)
- *"Warmi urquy": marriage proposals and gender hierarchy in the Peruvian Andes*, **Frontiers in Sociology**, March 2026 — [open access](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/sociology/articles/10.3389/fsoc.2026.1722698/full)
- *Shifting partnership ideals with online technologies among unmarried women in India*, **Social Forces**, July 2025 — [abstract](https://doi.org/10.1093/sf/soaf100)
